answer: The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 99 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. Because the timing is logged against the ocean challenge, the harbor audit can replay the basalt history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm thus has to pad 186 submissions and hold each member open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
